newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's anti-inflation fight to yield fruit - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy's anti-inflation fight to yield fruit - Fazio.

text.p: The governor of the Bank of Italy, Antonio Fazio, said on Tuesday the bank's tight monetary policy was aimed at eradicating inflation and benefits loomed.

"In the last four years, the stabilisation process has gained momentum and we are now in a position to reap the benefits," Fazio said in a speech prepared on the occasion of the Euromoney Central Banker of the Year award.
Fazio will receive the award on Tuesday in Washington. An advance copy of his speech was released in Rome.
"The tight monetary stance is aimed at eliminating once and for all the inflationary mentality that took hold in the seventies," Fazio said.
"A rigorous central bank strategy provides a framework of monetary stability that will foster economic stability."

Fazio's tight policy led to the bank maintaining official interest rates unchanged for more than a year before finally cutting the discount rate by 0.75 point in July to 8.25 percent after a fall in inflation.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, whose centre-left government has just presented a stringent 1997 budget designed to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit, and business leaders have called for another cut soon.
Fazio has indicated he wants to see inflation decline further first. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
